doc.title: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey Interview, 1959-03-15
doc.interviewee: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey

title: Chicago after the boat: George Fields and Freddie's group
summary: After the summer boat season he lands a job in Chicago with George Fields, then Freddie's five-piece, and plays a ballpark benefit.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well, I went to Chicago. See, it had to go fair. I went to Chicago out of Davenport. That's where we finished our summer season. And I had to either come by the way of St. Louis or Chicago to come back home. So I went to Chicago. And the first night I got a job with George Fields. And T.O.A. had just ran away from those. They left over that band and they had an opening. So they asked a fellow named Fernandez. Used to play with Dave Peet and they helped play with them. You know, after the show at the Grand Heath come and play with them at the Deluxe at 35th and State. When I went in there so they gave me a chance. I had never played with none of those guys but they knew of me through my family, you see. And so they gave me a chance up there and I played with them. I did all right. Until Manuel or Freddie came from Chicago, from New York. And he was a pretty good mixer, you know, a little better than Manuel. He used to spend all his money so he got the job. So the place closed down for repairs and Freddie went in there. Well, he went there with Tony Jackson and Noah Dutre and my cousin was on the drum Tubby. And let's see, there was five of those. There was five pieces. So I went back with him, asked George to leave me off and I went back in the place with Freddie. He said, well, if I get a job will you come with me? So I gave him my award, you know. So when he got a job down in the loop, at the beginning of the loop, 22nd War Bash, well I put Freddie in there and went with George. But the job didn't last long. It was a Fryberg place. That's an old place there right by the L train, 22nd War Bash. But it didn't last long and I believe I made my mistake there. I should have stayed with Freddie.
The time you played there at the ballpark, that picture was...

Well that was when I was working with Manuel and them. And Joe and them, they were playing the Royal, no, Joe was playing Bill Bata's Dreamland. And we made up, well all the bands were invited through the fans, you know, they paid our way, it wasn't with the dollars that were going, they paid our way. But we made more than that, we picked up about thirty-something dollars a piece in the park.
